beyondTheRegister: I asked what this change is for and what could make it wrong that no criterion names. It is a repair round, and the shape of its risk is that a repair introduces a fault the original did not have. Two of the thirteen repairs did exactly that, and both are the same one: the change adds three new readers of Account.timezone, and none of them carries the tolerance every shipped reader of that column carries. That is F1 and F2, and neither is visible to a UTC-run suite or to any test that seeds a valid zone.

findings.rule: sweep 11 — a mechanism applied at some call sites and not the rest
findings.claim: the new window code hands Account.timezone straight to Intl without the unknown-zone fallback every other reader of that column carries, so a stored zone that is not a resolvable identifier turns both feed routes into a permanent 500 for that member

witness.detail: The value is caller-supplied and unvalidated on two write paths. POST /api/invitations/accept is public and stores dto.timezone as any non-empty trimmed string (apps/api/src/invitations/invitations.service.ts:286-287, :293); PUT /api/account/settings stores it too, because validateTimezone only checks non-emptiness — `if (value.length === 0) return fail(...); return ok(value);` (packages/validation/src/index.ts:1060-1064) — and account.service.ts:96 writes the result. So an account can hold e.g. 'Europe/Warszawa' (a plausible typo the picker would never produce but the route accepts). That member then calls GET /api/organizations/{orgId}/portal/news. portal-feed.service.ts:134 calls todayInTimeZone, which catches the failure and answers the UTC date — its own comment is the mechanism: 'An unknown zone is a data anomaly, not a reason to fail a read; UTC is the same fallback a null zone gets' (packages/validation/src/requests.ts:648-651). Line 135 then calls computePortalWindow(today, caller.timezone); the guard at portal-entry.types.ts:138 only rescues null and blank, so the raw string reaches zonedTimeToUtc -> zoneOffsetMs -> zonedParts -> partsFormatter, which constructs `new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', { timeZone })` with no try/catch (packages/validation/src/hiring-time.ts:31-44, :77, :96, :127-129). Verified by command: `node -e "new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US',{timeZone:'Not/AZone',hourCycle:'h23',year:'numeric'})"` prints `THROWS: RangeError Invalid time zone specified: Not/AZone`, while the en-CA formatter todayInTimeZone builds throws the same error and is caught. Nothing above catches it, so the route answers 500 on every read, and portal-entry.service.ts:63 makes every entry page 500 the same way. Before this attempt the same account read the feed normally, because computePortalWindow only concatenated strings. The mechanism is the repository's, not an invention: the other shared reader of this column states it as a rule — 'An empty / unknown / UTC zone — or any Intl failure — falls back to UTC' (packages/validation/src/index.ts:2994-2998, implemented at :2999-3016).

findings.suggestedFix: resolve the zone once through the same tolerance the rest of the codebase uses — fall back to 'UTC' when isValidTimeZone(zone) is false (packages/validation/src/hiring-time.ts:54-62) before either zonedTimeToUtc call, so an unresolvable stored zone reads the window in UTC exactly as todayInTimeZone already reads the date

findings.rule: sweep 11 — a mechanism applied at some call sites and not the rest
findings.claim: the feed's new zone plumbing reads session.account.timezone with a weaker guard than every shipped screen that reads the same field and then constructs Intl directly, so an unresolvable stored zone throws during render and the home screen shows an error instead of the feed

witness.detail: Same input as F1 — an account whose timezone was stored through POST /api/invitations/accept (invitations.service.ts:286-287) or PUT /api/account/settings (validateTimezone, packages/validation/src/index.ts:1060-1064) as any non-empty string. /api/me answers the column raw (apps/api/src/members/me.controller.ts:110). PortalFeed.tsx:298 does `session.account.timezone ?? 'UTC'`, which passes a non-null unresolvable identifier straight through, and localYmd (:88-90) constructs `new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-CA', { timeZone })` with no try/catch. It is reached on the ordinary path: groupByDay (:135) calls dayLabel (:126) for every entry as soon as the feed answers with at least one, so the component throws during render and React unwinds to the nearest error boundary — the whole /org/{orgId} screen, not just the feed column, which is the opposite of the independence contracts §States requires of the two halves. formatRelativeTime (:113-114) does the same twice more. The four shipped screens that read this exact field all guard it before use — `session.account.timezone && session.account.timezone.trim().length > 0 ? … : 'UTC'` at time-tracking/page.tsx:76-78, TimerBar.tsx:67-69, reports/time-and-activity/page.tsx:122-124, reports/amounts-owed/page.tsx:86-88 — and hand the value to wallClockParts, which swallows any Intl failure and returns UTC parts (packages/validation/src/index.ts:2999-3016). The new reader carries neither half of that mechanism.

findings.suggestedFix: resolve the zone once at PortalFeed.tsx:298 with the guard the other four screens use and fall back to 'UTC' when isValidTimeZone is false, so no Intl constructor in this file can be handed a string the engine refuses

findings.rule: sweep 8 — an assertion that cannot fail for the defect its own comment claims it catches
findings.claim: the new right-edge probe cannot see an untruncated title, contrary to the comment beside it

witness.detail: portal.spec.ts:417-420 says 'A long title that was not truncated (the defect this case is also built to catch) would push that cell out of place.' It would not. The row is `gridTemplateColumns: 'minmax(0,1fr) auto auto'` (PortalRequestsPanel.tsx:33) and the title sits inside the first track's grid item, itself `minWidth: 0` (:89). A `<b>` left at display:inline with white-space:nowrap — precisely the state before this attempt's one-line fix at :43 — overflows its containing block with overflow:visible; it contributes nothing to the 1fr track's minimum, which is 0, so the auto tracks and the badge's right edge are exactly where they were. The probe passes either way. The left-edge probe above it is the one doing the work.

findings.suggestedFix: either delete the claim from the comment, or assert the truncation directly — compare the `<b>`'s clientWidth against its scrollWidth on the 200-character row
